_notes: PROSE THE GAME SAYS OUTSIDE A SCRIPTED SCENE (owner rule 2026-08-05:
story elements must not be embedded in code). Everything here used to be
a string literal in a .gd file, which meant a writer could not change a
word without editing a program, and no content tool could see it.
Keys are dotted paths. Values are a string or an array of lines. %s and
%d placeholders are filled positionally by Strings.line/lines -- keep the
order and the count when rewriting, tests/unit/test_strings.gd checks
that every key the code asks for exists and takes the arguments given.
Scene prose does NOT live here -- that is story/prologue/ and the
quests' own steps. This file is the game's own voice: the prowl's
book-keeping, the chronicle's event lines, and the room's captions.

press_on.earned: SATCHEL: %d gleam, up %d. Gleam is what the city pays for trouble taken off its hands — and the satchel is not yours until you carry it home.
press_on.wager: Deeper pays better. Deeper also bites.

finish: Done. %d gleam banked — %d out of the satchel, %d for the trouble.
The Mantel waits. So does the thread.
retreat: Home by the gutters. %d gleam banked.
prowl.retreat_dropped: %d gleam went over the wall without me. You cannot run and hold.
prowl.retreat_tail: The quest keeps. Quests do. It is one of their few virtues.
prowl.toll: The Toll: %d gleam. The satchel stays wherever you dropped it.
prowl.journal_prologue: The night the kettle screamed. Elspeth is gone. The thread leads into the city.

chronicle.walked_in: Walked in. Sometimes the front door is the trick.
chronicle.concentrate: Ash stares at nothing. A %s comes back — next turn.
chronicle.sunbeam: A sunbeam. One spent card returns, warm.
chronicle.warmed: Still warm from the purr: +2 HP.
chronicle.sharpened: Claws keen from a clean fight: +1 first hit.
chronicle.hidden_wasted: It strikes at the shadow you left behind.
chronicle.approach_stalk: You are a rumor in the dark.
chronicle.approach_case: You watch. You learn. You draw.
chronicle.approach_ward: A ward, stitched quick and holding.
chronicle.parting_shot: You turn your back. It takes its turn anyway.
chronicle.loaf_guarded: It paws at a cat with nothing loose. Nothing gives.
chronicle.night_presses: The night presses. It grows bolder.
chronicle.undone: It finishes the sentence it started.

mantel.board_empty: Nothing pinned tonight. The city is being quiet at you.
mantel.no_deeds: The thread runs out under the window.

exchange: Brindle. Cards and tonics, sold sharp.

title.name: THE NINE LIVES OF ASHCAT
title.prologue_done: Prologue complete. The Mantel is open.

_notes: THE CASEBOOK'S RECORD OF WHAT THE PLAYER HAS DONE.
core/chronicle.gd stores FACTS -- a kind, the ids involved, the numbers
involved. These are the sentences those facts are rendered into, at the
moment the Casebook is opened rather than at the moment the thing
happened. Rewrite a line here and every past entry re-reads with the new
wording; there is no migration, because no sentence was ever stored.
Three of these used to be string literals inside game.gd (law 20).
Keys MUST match Chronicle.KINDS exactly -- tests/unit/test_chronicle.gd
fails on a kind with no template and on a template with no kind. The %s
and %d placeholders are filled positionally in the order that file
declares: ids first, then texts, then numbers.
chronicle_log.prologue_done: The night the kettle screamed. Elspeth is gone. The thread leads into the city.
chronicle_log.life_spent: Spent a life to %s. The Court noted it.
chronicle_log.favor_tied: A knot in the thread: %s owes me.

_approach_notes: An approach's PRICE is a rule and lives in data/rules.json; its NAME
and what it reads like are writing and live here (law 20). The names
were a `name` field inside CombatState.APPROACHES until 2026-08-05,
which meant renaming 'Case It' meant editing a rules engine.

approach.stalk: Begin hidden. Its first move misses. First hit +1.
approach.ambush: Strike first for 3. It comes up angry.
approach.case: Study it, draw 2 — it studies you back: +1 first hit.
approach.ward: Block 4 that holds through its first turn.
approach.walk_in_desc: Spend nothing. A door is a door.

battle.withdraw_default: This is not a fight. It is weather. Go around it.
battle.concentrate_desc: Give up the whole turn to will one spent energy back onto the TOP OF THE DECK — you draw it next turn, not now. The enemy still moves. Twice a fight.
battle.card_desc: Energy powers your actions — tap an action card below to feed this to it. Spent energy is gone until you rest at home.

exchange.greeting: 'Everything shines to somebody, pet. Have a look at what fell off the world this week.'

plain: An honest first of any humour.
add: A second — twice a plain card.
tonic: A swallow of health. Tastes of pond.

patter.plain: 'The everyday stuff. The city runs on it.'
patter.rare: 'Ah. The good shelf. For a discerning paw.'
patter.no_more_tonic: 'You are one cat. There are limits. That was the last one.'
patter.tonic: 'Drink it all. Yes, it tastes like pond. Medicinal pond.'
patter.bought_card: 'A fine choice. It fell off a windowsill, if anyone asks.'
patter.broke: 'Sentiment is lovely. Gleam is lovelier. Come back shinier.'

popup.tonic_rule: %d more health, up to a ceiling of %d. He stands at %d now.
popup.spend_body: %s, for %d gleam. She is already reaching for it.

loadout.slots_heading: What goes out with you — %d, and Scratch is always one
loadout.bench_empty: Nothing left on the mantel — everything Ash knows is going with him.

spool.title: The Spool
spool.blurb: Every card you own keeps at home. Wind on what should go out with him — changing your mind is free, and nothing is ever lost.
spool.count: %d on the spool · %d kept at home
spool.floor: The spool runs no thinner than %d.

skill.always: Scratch goes where Ash goes. It is not a choice, which is the kindest thing about it.

shared by the battle close-up and the loadout close-up. Keys damage /

skill_rules.channel_heal: Heal %d per turn for %d turns. Ash lies still until it ends — taking damage breaks it
skill_rules.self_stun: You cannot act next turn — and nothing can be stolen from your paws
